title: Enhancing Large Language Models for Mobility Analytics with Semantic Location Tokenization

problem.claim: The work targets modeling user movement dynamics and mobility analytics with large language models.

gap.claim: Existing methods inadequately represent locations semantically and insufficiently model mobility signals because they rely on discrete location IDs and single templated-instruction fine-tuning.

contributions.claim: QT-Mob is a framework for enhancing large language models for mobility analytics.
Its location tokenization module learns compact, semantically rich location tokens that preserve contextual information and remain compatible with large language models.
It uses complementary fine-tuning objectives to align learned tokens with internal large-language-model representations and model sequential movement patterns and location semantics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe QT-Mob as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance on next-location prediction and mobility recovery across three real-world datasets compared with existing deep learning and large-language-model methods.
The authors report that QT-Mob provides a more generalizable approach for various mobility analytics tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Location-based services generate large volumes of mobility data relevant to modeling urban movement dynamics.
Recent work has adapted large language models for mobility analytics.
Existing approaches have weak semantic location representation and limited mobility-signal modeling.
QT-Mob combines semantic location tokenization with complementary fine-tuning objectives aligned to large-language-model representations.
The authors report improved performance on next-location prediction and mobility recovery across three real-world datasets.
